Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark, dark brown to black circular spots with characteristic concentric 'target' rings on older lower leaves, causing eventual yellowing and leaf drop.
treatment: Prune and destroy heavily infected lower leaves immediately to slow the upward migration of spores
Apply preventative or therapeutic fungicides containing chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or copper compounds
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Implement a strict 2-to-3-year crop rotation omitting other nightshades, maximize plant spacing, and mulch well to prevent soil splashing.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: Stems are upright and strong; foliage is evenly green and free from necrotic lesions, spotting, or premature wilting.
Potato___healthy.prevention: Ensure consistent soil moisture without waterlogging, provide adequate hilling, and monitor fields weekly.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked dark lesions on leaves and stems that quickly rot; a white, velvety fungal growth appears on the undersides of leaves during cool, humid weather.
treatment: Quickly pull and destroy entire infected plants to prevent rapid airborne field devastation
Apply specialized protectant fungicides such as mancozeb, chlorothalonil, or systemic oomycete treatments to surrounding healthy rows
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Plant only certified disease-free seed tubers, avoid overhead watering to minimize leaf wetness periods, and destroy any volunteer potato plants or cull piles.
